Shaping the Future, One Girl at a Time
Welcome to Glendower Preparatory School – a place where girls are empowered to flourish academically, socially and personally. Since 1895, we have been dedicated to educating bright young women, with a long-standing commitment to exceptional learning and a tradition of challenging expectations.
Start Her Glendower Story
"I think the academic and preparation aspect of Glendower is unrivalled. The girls I meet who are in Year 5 and 6 are intelligent, engaged and confident."
"I love the warm inclusive environment at Glendower. It makes me feel very comfortable with all of the girls. I also feel like it’s a safe space and a second home to me."
"I have loved the teachers in every class that my daughter has been in. It’s clear they really care. The girls are all very confident and I think the school encourages individuality."
"What I love most about my school is that we are all in one community no matter who you are."
"Our daughter has been very happy since reception. She has a good friend group, and the school has been doing amazingly well in making sure the girls are kind and confident."
"Glendower was founded with a mission to provide an academically ambitious and intellectually un-compromising education to girls. […] It is clear this mission remains central."

pageCache.text:
Our Ethos, Aims and Values
IN 100 WORDS
At Glendower, our ethos - Living in the moment. Looking to the future. - underpins everything we do. We celebrate the joy of childhood while preparing girls with the confidence, character and skills to thrive in an ever-changing world. Guided by our four aims; Girls First, Proudly Academic, Living Lightly & Fully, and Being Gamechangers in Society, we nurture confident, curious and compassionate learners who think independently, lead with integrity and make a positive impact. These principles are brought to life through our values: Responsibility, Readiness, Resourcefulness, Resilience, Reflection, Relationships and Respect – the 7Rs that are known well across our school.
Ethos
Glendower’s ethos is: Living in the moment. Looking to the future. This core philosophy shapes the the experience of every girl at Glendower and informs the way we think about education - not only as preparation for exams, but as preparation for life. We treasure the joy of childhood, encouraging our pupils to embrace every opportunity for joy, challenge or discovery whilst equipping them with the confidence, character and skills to thrive in an ever-changing world.
We are unapologetically ambitious for our pupils. We believe in the transformative power of girls' education and in creating an environment where girls can think freely, lead confidently and develop a strong sense of self, ensuring they leave Glendower ready not only for the next stage of their education, but to shape the future with purpose.
Aims
Our ethos is upheld through four guiding principles, our aims:
Girls First Everything we do begins with a deep understanding of girls: how they learn, how they grow and how they thrive. In an environment designed specifically for them, our pupils develop confidence in their voice, their ideas and their identity. They are encouraged to take intellectual risks, to lead without hesitation and to see themselves as capable of shaping the world around them.
Proudly Academic Academic excellence is at the heart of a Glendower education. We offer a rich, ambitious and carefully sequenced curriculum that challenges and inspires. Our girls are taught to think critically, to question deeply and to take pride in their scholarship. We foster a culture where effort, curiosity and intellectual rigour are both expected and celebrated.
Living Lightly & Fully We believe that education should develop the whole child. Our girls learn to move through the world with kindness, awareness and a strong sense of responsibility for their actions. At the same time, they are encouraged to embrace opportunity, explore their interests and participate fully in school life, across sport, the arts and beyond.
Being Gamechangers in Society We aspire for our pupils to leave Glendower ready to make a difference. They develop the courage, resilience and integrity needed to contribute meaningfully to society. With a strong sense of citizenship and social responsibility, they are equipped to challenge, to lead and to create positive change in the world around them.
These principles are lived daily, in our classrooms, in our relationships and in the wider life of the school. They are underpinned by high expectations, strong pastoral care and a deep commitment to every girl’s success and wellbeing.
Values
Our values reflect the character traits we expect each girl to develop in her time with us. Our pupils know these as the 7Rs:
The 7Rs are a routine part of life at Glendower, forming the basis for assemblies, awards and classroom expectations.

Strategic Vision
IN 100 WORDS
Shaping the Future One Girl at a Time is our ambitious vision for the future of the school.
Grounded in our belief in the transformative power of girls’ education, it sets out a clear and purposeful direction built on four pillars: Driving Academic Excellence, Inspiring Innovation, Nurturing Wellbeing & Community, and Future Proofing Our Legacy.
Together, these priorities ensure that Glendower continues to offer an exceptional education, one that is intellectually rigorous, forward-thinking and deeply rooted in strong values, preparing every girl to thrive in a rapidly changing world.
Shaping the Future One Girl at a Time
Driving Academic Excellence
We are unapologetically academic. This pillar focuses on strengthening an already ambitious curriculum, ensuring depth of understanding, high expectations and outstanding outcomes for every pupil. We are committed to developing confident thinkers who approach learning with curiosity, discipline and intellectual rigour.
Inspiring Innovation
Education must continually evolve. We are committed to embracing innovation in teaching, curriculum design and the use of technology, ensuring that our pupils are equipped with the skills, knowledge and adaptability required for the future. This includes fostering creativity, critical thinking and an openness to new ideas.
Nurturing Wellbeing & Community
A successful education is built on strong relationships and a deep sense of belonging. This pillar focuses on strengthening our pastoral care, supporting pupil wellbeing and continuing to build a connected, inclusive and values-driven community. We believe that when girls feel safe, supported and understood, they are able to achieve their very best.
Future Proofing Our Legacy
As we look ahead, we are committed to ensuring the long-term sustainability and growth of Glendower. This includes investment in our people, our environment and our facilities, alongside careful strategic planning that secures the school’s future for generations to come.
Together, these four pillars provide a clear and coherent framework for the next chapter of Glendower’s journey. They ensure that we remain both rooted in our heritage and responsive to the future, combining tradition with ambition, and stability with forward momentum.

Head’s Welcome
IN 100 WORDS
Welcome to Glendower Preparatory School. This is a place where intellectual curiosity, ambition and character are nurtured in equal measure. We are unapologetically committed to academic excellence and to the transformative power of girls’ education.
At Glendower, we believe that a rigorous education, rooted in strong relationships and a deep understanding of how children learn, enables every girl to flourish. Our girls leave us as confident thinkers, articulate communicators and kind, purposeful young people who are ready not only for the next stage of their education, but for life beyond it.
It is a privilege to welcome you to Glendower Preparatory School.
Glendower is a school with a proud history and a clear sense of purpose. We are deeply committed to providing an education that is both intellectually rigorous and profoundly human, one that recognises the unique potential of every girl and equips her to thrive in an ever-changing world.
Our belief in the transformative power of girls’ education sits at the heart of everything we do. In a setting designed specifically for them, girls are empowered to think boldly, to lead with confidence and to develop a strong sense of self. They learn to use their voice, to challenge ideas and to engage deeply with the world around them.
Academic excellence is not simply an aspiration at Glendower; it is a lived reality. Our curriculum is ambitious, carefully sequenced and enriched by specialist teaching. We place great importance on depth of understanding, critical thinking and intellectual curiosity. From the earliest years, our pupils are encouraged to ask questions, make connections and take pride in their scholarship.
Alongside this, we are equally committed to the development of character. We understand that education is not only about what girls know, but who they become. Through strong relationships, high expectations and a culture of kindness and respect, we nurture resilience, integrity and empathy in every girl.
As Head, I feel a deep sense of responsibility, and optimism, about the role education plays in shaping the future. At Glendower, we are not only preparing girls for the next stage of their education; we are preparing them to lead meaningful, purposeful lives.
I hope this website offers you a sense of our values, our ambition and the spirit of our school. We would be delighted to welcome you to Glendower and to share more of what makes this such a special place to learn, grow and succeed.

Community Partnerships
IN 100 WORDS
Through meaningful partnerships with local schools, charities and community organisations, our girls develop empathy, social awareness and a sense of responsibility for the world around them. From our award-winning GlenSpark programme to intergenerational projects and charitable initiatives, our girls discover the value of collaboration, service and leadership.
Together, these experiences inspire every girl to become a compassionate citizen and a positive force for change within her community.
At Glendower, we believe that education carries with it a responsibility to contribute positively to society. Our community partnerships provide meaningful opportunities for girls to engage with the wider world, developing empathy, confidence and a deeper understanding of the difference they can make.
Central to this work is GlenSpark, our award-winning partnership programme that brings together pupils from Glendower and local primary schools. Through collaborative projects, public speaking events, academic workshops and shared learning experiences, pupils work alongside children from different backgrounds, learning from one another while developing confidence, communication skills and mutual respect. GlenSpark reflects our belief that the very best education is enriched through collaboration, curiosity and the exchange of ideas.
Our commitment to partnership extends across the local community. Girls regularly build relationships with residents of local care homes through visits, shared celebrations and intergenerational activities that foster kindness, understanding and connection. These experiences help pupils develop empathy, appreciate different life experiences and recognise the importance of community across generations.
Supporting charitable causes is another important part of life at Glendower. Throughout the year, our take part in fundraising initiatives, awareness campaigns and community projects that encourage them to think beyond themselves and consider the needs of others. Whether supporting local organisations or responding to national and global appeals, girls learn that even small acts of kindness can have a meaningful impact.These experiences are carefully woven into the wider life of the school and reflect our commitment to developing socially aware, compassionate young people. They encourage girls to become active participants in their communities, understanding that leadership is not only about achievement but also about service, responsibility and making a positive difference.

Introduction to Little Glendower Nursery
IN 100 WORDS
Little Glendower Nursery is where a lifelong love of learning begins. For girls aged 2 to 4, we provide a warm, nurturing and stimulating environment where curiosity is encouraged and confidence begins to grow. Through carefully structured play, early exploration and strong relationships, our youngest pupils develop the foundations for future learning.
With a focus on communication, independence and social development, we ensure that every girl feels known, valued and ready to thrive as they take their first steps into school life.
Little Glendower Nursery offers a joyful and purposeful start to each girl’s educational journey. For our youngest pupils, aged 2 to 4, these early years are a time of rapid development, discovery and growth.
We create an environment in which every child feels safe, known and valued. Strong relationships sit at the heart of our nursery, enabling girls to build confidence, develop a sense of belonging and approach new experiences with curiosity and enthusiasm.
Our approach is carefully designed to balance play and purpose. Through structured and exploratory activities, children develop key early skills in communication, language, early mathematics and physical development. We place particular emphasis on developing strong foundations in speaking and listening, recognising these as critical to future academic success.
Alongside this, we nurture independence from the very beginning. Girls are encouraged to make choices, explore their interests and begin to take ownership of their learning in age-appropriate ways. Through this, they develop confidence, resilience and a growing sense of self.
Learning at Little Glendower extends beyond the classroom. Through creative play, music, movement and outdoor exploration, children experience a rich and varied curriculum that supports their development across all areas. Each day brings opportunities for imagination, collaboration and discovery.
To find out more about our Nursery, please visit our nursery admissions page

pageCache.text:
Ahead of the Curve: How Glendower’s GlenX Curriculum Reflects the Future of Education
This week, I listened with great interest to the interview with Bridget Phillipson, Secretary of State for Education, on BBC Radio 4’s Today programme. The conversation marked the government’s response to the year-long curriculum and assessment review led by Professor Becky Francis, a comprehensive piece of work exploring how education in England can evolve to prepare young people more effectively for the modern world.
Described as one of the most wide-ranging reviews in a generation, the report offers a candid and constructive reflection on the current state of schooling. It recognises that while our education system has long been successful in promoting academic achievement, it has not always kept pace with the broader competencies needed to thrive in a world shaped by rapid technological, social, and environmental change.
The review’s central message is clear: education must move beyond a narrow focus on examination performance to develop young people who can think critically, communicate effectively, solve complex problems, and navigate the ethical and digital challenges of the 21st century. It advocates a recalibration of priorities, one that values intellectual curiosity, creativity, and resilience alongside knowledge and academic attainment.
While the recommendations are directed primarily at the maintained sector and at secondary education, their implications reach far wider. The direction of travel they outline, towards more adaptable, future-ready learning, is one that all schools, independent and maintained alike, must engage with.
Alignment with Glendower’s Vision
It was both heartening and affirming to hear this national conversation echo so strongly the principles that underpin our own strategic vision at Glendower. Over the past year, we have been deliberately and thoughtfully evolving our curriculum to ensure that our girls develop not only strong academic foundations, but also the intellectual agility, digital discernment, and global awareness they will need for the future.
This work culminated in the launch of our new GlenX: Future Skills programme in September 2025, an innovation designed for all Prep pupils in Years 3 to 6. GlenX represents the next step in our mission to shape the future, one girl at a time.
Where the Francis Review calls for education to reimagine its relationship with knowledge, technology, and creativity, GlenX offers a living example of that vision in action. Our GlenX curriculum is built around four key strands, each chosen to equip our pupils with the skills, understanding, and mindset to thrive in a rapidly changing world:
Through GlenX, pupils explore these concepts in an integrated, age-appropriate way, making connections across subjects and real-world contexts. They learn to debate, question, build, and create, developing both the intellectual habits and the character strengths that underpin lifelong learning.
Ahead of the National Curve
What is particularly encouraging is how closely GlenX aligns with the review’s key themes, from digital fluency to critical thinking, sustainability, and communication. The report calls for schools to embed these dimensions not as “add-ons” but as central to what it means to be educated. That philosophy sits at the heart of GlenX.
It also reaffirms something we have long believed at Glendower: that primary education has a uniquely powerful role to play in laying the foundations for these future-ready competencies. The habits of curiosity, empathy, and resilience developed in these early years form the scaffolding for everything that follows.
We are proud, therefore, that Glendower is not waiting for national reform to dictate direction, but leading the way, designing a curriculum that reflects both the challenges and the possibilities of the century ahead.
Continuous Reflection and Renewal
As with all meaningful innovation, GlenX will continue to evolve. We are committed to ongoing reflection, listening to our pupils’ experiences, drawing on the expertise of our staff, and keeping pace with the changing educational landscape. In doing so, we remain true to our school’s founding purpose: to provide an education that not only informs the mind but also inspires the heart.
As the government embarks on this new phase of curriculum reform, I take great pride in knowing that Glendower is already demonstrating what such a vision can look like in practice. Through GlenX, we are empowering our girls to be thinkers, creators, collaborators, and changemakers, ready not only to meet the future, but to shape it.

pageCache.pageTitle: Stories: Glendower’s 130th Anniversary Art Exhibition - Glendower Preparatory School
pageCache.text:
Stories: Glendower’s 130th Anniversary Art Exhibition
Our 130th Anniversary celebrations culminated this week in a spectacular exhibition of pupil artwork entitled Stories. It was a joy to welcome so many parents and carers to celebrate the imagination, talent, and hard work of our young artists.
Throughout the term, Miss Jones guided the girls through the creation of both collaborative and independent projects that explored an inspiring range of themes, materials, and artistic styles. These formed the basis of our exhibition.
The Nursery children began their artistic journeys by experimenting with colour and shape while learning about the colour wheel. Inspired by Pablo Picasso’s bold use of colour and abstract form, their collaborative piece bursts with movement and energy – a joyful painting full of expressive, funny faces.
Reception invited visitors to wander through their stepping-stone garden, a work born from their fascination with nature and plants. Drawing inspiration from the Barbican Conservatory, the children painted vibrant designs on acrylic stones to create their own miniature installation.
Year 1 channelled the playful abstraction of Paul Klee in their imaginative self-portraits. Using pastels and a variety of 3D materials, the children layered colour, texture, and form to create a vibrant collage celebrating individuality and creativity.
Year 2 embraced the art of weaving through a collaborative textile piece inspired by Anni Albers. Experimenting with bold geometric patterns and richly coloured fibres, they worked together to interlace threads into rhythmic, layered designs that highlight teamwork and artistic tradition.
Year 3 turned their attention to the architecture of South Kensington and beyond. Their intricate watercolour and pen studies capture the textures, shapes, and details of our cityscape through the fresh eyes of young artists.
Year 4 produced colourful diptychs inspired by Henri Matisse, combining oil pastels and paper collage to tell stories in two distinct mediums. Their work explores how different materials can evoke a spectrum of emotions from a single subject.
Year 5 explored storytelling through personal memory, transforming moments from their own lives into expressive acrylic paintings. Some chose realism to recreate vivid memories, while others used stylised approaches to convey emotion and atmosphere – together, their work forms a moving collection of personal narratives.
Year 6’s self-portraits paid homage to Frida Kahlo, weaving symbols of nature and emotion into powerful compositions. Using colour and value with sensitivity, their paintings express stories of growth, resilience, and self-reflection.
Finally, Miss Jones and the Art Scholars presented a series of vibrant canvases inspired by Aboriginal artist Emily Kame Kngwarreye. Echoing her flowing lines, bold colours, and rich textures, each piece reflects a personal journey – a visual expression of the experiences, memories, and stories that shape us all.
Stories was a fitting finale to our anniversary celebrations; a joyful testament to creativity, collaboration, and the enduring power of art to connect us across generations.
For 130 years, Glendower Prep School has nurtured the curiosity, confidence, and creativity of girls, empowering them to express their voices and shape their own stories. This exhibition continues that legacy, reminding us that while our world has changed, the spirit of Glendower – one of imagination, courage, and a love of learning – remains constant. Through each brushstroke, sculpture, and collage, our pupils have not only celebrated the past but also looked boldly toward the future, carrying forward the values that have defined Glendower for more than a century: excellence, self-expression, and joy in discovery!

Wellbeing Curriculum
IN 100 WORDS
At Glendower, wellbeing is not an initiative, it is an essential part of education.
Our carefully sequenced wellbeing curriculum equips girls with the knowledge, skills and strategies to understand themselves, build positive relationships and navigate life's challenges with confidence. Through dedicated teaching, an in-house Mindset Coach and a culture of care, we develop resilient, reflective and emotionally intelligent young people who are ready to flourish both in school and beyond.
We believe that wellbeing is fundamental to successful learning and personal growth. Just as we explicitly teach reading, writing and mathematics, we believe that the knowledge, skills and habits that support emotional wellbeing should also be taught deliberately and progressively.
Our wellbeing curriculum is carefully designed to help girls understand themselves, develop healthy relationships and build the confidence to navigate challenge with resilience and optimism. As pupils grow, they develop emotional literacy, self-awareness and the ability to reflect thoughtfully on their experiences, enabling them to become increasingly independent and confident learners.
The curriculum is delivered through dedicated PSHE and RSE lessons, pastoral education and the everyday experiences of school life. Topics are thoughtfully sequenced to ensure they are developmentally appropriate, allowing pupils to explore themes such as friendships, emotional regulation, digital wellbeing, identity, belonging and healthy decision-making in a safe and supportive environment.
A distinctive feature of our provision is our in-house Mindset Coach, who works alongside pupils, staff and families to develop positive learning behaviours, resilience and confidence. Through individual coaching, small-group sessions and whole-school initiatives, girls learn practical strategies for approaching challenge, managing setbacks and developing a positive, growth-oriented mindset.
Our approach is grounded in the belief that resilience is developed through experience, reflection and support. We encourage girls to embrace challenge, learn from mistakes and recognise that perseverance and effort are key to long-term success. In doing so, they develop the confidence to tackle increasingly complex academic and personal challenges with courage and self-belief.

Creative Arts
IN 100 WORDS
The creative arts are central to a Glendower education.
Through art, music, drama and performance, pupils develop creativity, technical skill and the confidence to express themselves with authenticity. Alongside specialist teaching and high expectations, girls are encouraged to create, perform and collaborate, discovering the joy of artistic expression while developing resilience, imagination and presence.
Whether on the stage, in the studio or in the concert hall, every girl is given the opportunity to find her voice and realise her creative potential.
The creative arts are an essential part of life at Glendower. Through art, music, drama and performance, our girls learn to think imaginatively, communicate confidently and express themselves with authenticity.
Our creative arts curriculum is carefully sequenced, enabling girls to develop both technical proficiency and creative confidence as they progress through the school. Specialist teaching ensures that pupils build strong foundations while being challenged to refine their skills, experiment with new ideas and develop their own artistic voice.
In art, pupils explore a wide range of media, techniques and artistic traditions, developing both practical skills and an appreciation of visual culture. They are encouraged to observe carefully, think creatively and produce work that reflects both technical understanding and individual expression.
Music is a vibrant part of school life. Through curriculum lessons, choirs, ensembles, one-to-one instrumental tuition and regular performances, pupils develop musicianship, confidence and a lifelong appreciation of music. Whether singing as part of a choir, performing as a soloist or learning a new instrument, every girl is encouraged to participate and strive for excellence.
Drama and performance provide opportunities for pupils to develop creativity, communication and self-confidence. Through informal performances, large scale productions, public speaking and collaborative projects, girls learn to interpret, create and perform with increasing confidence, developing skills that extend far beyond the stage.
Performance is woven throughout the life of the school. Concerts, exhibitions, productions, assemblies and celebrations provide regular opportunities for every pupil to share her talents with others. These experiences cultivate resilience, presence and the confidence to perform before an audience, while celebrating the creativity and individuality of every girl.

Learning & Pedagogy
IN 100 WORDS
Exceptional teaching lies at the heart of a Glendower education.
Our pedagogy is grounded in research, shaped by expertise and informed by a deep understanding of how girls learn and thrive. We combine academic rigour with high-quality relationships, creating classrooms where curiosity is nurtured, challenge is embraced and every girl is encouraged to think deeply, contribute confidently and achieve her very best.
Through ambitious teaching and purposeful learning experiences, we inspire girls not simply to succeed in school, but to develop the habits of mind that will serve them throughout their lives.
At Glendower, we believe that great schools are built on great teaching. Our pedagogy is the deliberate craft of how we teach, designed to ensure that every lesson challenges, inspires and enables girls to flourish.
As specialists in girls' education, we recognise that effective teaching is about far more than delivering knowledge. It is about understanding how girls develop confidence, resilience and intellectual independence, and creating learning environments in which every pupil feels both supported and challenged to achieve her very best.
Our teaching is informed by educational research, cognitive science and a commitment to continual professional development. We know that pupils learn best when new knowledge is carefully sequenced, regularly revisited and connected to what they already know. We use questioning to deepen thinking, feedback to move learning forward and assessment to inform teaching rather than simply measure it.
Academic ambition underpins every classroom. We believe all girls deserve to experience the challenge and satisfaction of thinking deeply. Lessons are characterised by high expectations, rich dialogue and purposeful collaboration, encouraging pupils to analyse, debate, create and solve problems with increasing confidence and sophistication.
Equally important are the relationships that make great learning possible. Our teachers know every girl exceptionally well, recognising when to stretch, when to support and when to encourage greater independence. We foster classrooms where mistakes are viewed as opportunities to learn, effort is celebrated and girls are encouraged to develop the confidence to ask questions, share ideas and persevere when learning becomes challenging.
This is what it means to be proudly academic at Glendower. We cultivate scholarship without elitism, ambition without unnecessary pressure and excellence within a culture of warmth and belonging.

pageCache.pageTitle: Learning Support & Neurodiversity - Glendower Preparatory School
pageCache.text:
Learning Support & Neurodiversity
IN 100 WORDS
At Glendower, we recognise that every girl learns differently.
Our approach to learning support and neurodiversity is rooted in understanding the individual. Through early identification, expert guidance and personalised support, we ensure that every pupil is equipped to thrive academically, socially and emotionally. Working closely with families, teachers and external specialists where appropriate, we celebrate each girl's unique strengths while providing the strategies and support that enable her to flourish with confidence.
At Glendower, we believe that every girl should be known, understood and supported to fulfil her potential. As specialists in girls' education, we recognise that there is no single way to learn and that understanding how each child learns best is fundamental to academic success and personal wellbeing.
Our approach to learning support is built upon early identification, close collaboration and personalised provision. Through careful observation, ongoing assessment and regular dialogue between teachers, families and our specialist staff, we develop a detailed understanding of each pupil's individual strengths, needs and learning profile.
We embrace neurodiversity as a natural and valuable part of our school community. Girls with a range of learning profiles are supported to develop confidence in themselves as learners, recognising both the challenges they may face and the unique strengths they bring. Our aim is not simply to remove barriers to learning, but to empower every pupil to become an independent, resilient and successful learner.
Our specialist team works in close partnership with teachers to ensure that inclusive practice is embedded across every classroom. This collaborative approach ensures that pupils receive consistent support while continuing to experience the high expectations and academic ambition that define a Glendower education.

Sport
IN 100 WORDS
Sport is an integral part of a Glendower education, developing confident, resilient and active young women.
Through specialist teaching, exceptional facilities and an ambitious programme of curriculum sport, fixtures and enrichment, every girl is encouraged to discover her strengths, embrace challenge and experience the joy of physical activity. Whether representing the school, leading a team or trying a sport for the first time, our girls develop the confidence, character and skills to lead healthy, active lives long beyond their years at Glendower.
At Glendower, we believe that sport and physical education are fundamental to every girl's education. More than developing sporting ability, our programme builds confidence, resilience, teamwork and leadership, fostering a lifelong enjoyment of physical activity and healthy living.
Our vision is not simply to develop outstanding athletes, but to ensure that every girl leaves Glendower with the skills, confidence and enthusiasm to enjoy sport throughout her life. We know that girls who develop positive experiences of physical activity in childhood are more likely to remain active as they grow older, and our curriculum is designed with this long-term ambition in mind.
Our ambitious physical education curriculum is delivered by specialist teachers and carefully sequenced to develop knowledge, skills and confidence at every stage. Pupils begin by mastering fundamental movement skills before progressing to health-related fitness, games, gymnastics, swimming and athletics. Specialist units, including climbing in Year 4, encourage girls to embrace challenge, develop resilience and discover new strengths.
Sport flourishes both on and beyond our South Kensington site. Pupils benefit from outstanding facilities at Imperial College and our 26-acre home sports ground at BEST in Barnes, where they enjoy high-quality coaching across netball, football, cricket and athletics. These exceptional facilities enable us to offer a breadth and quality of sporting provision that is unusual for a central London preparatory school.
Every girl has the opportunity to represent Glendower through our fully inclusive fixture programme from Years 3 to 6. Competition is viewed as an opportunity for growth, encouraging pupils to compete with determination, humility and respect. Leadership is woven throughout our sporting culture, from Year 6 House Captains leading inter-house competitions to weekly team reflections that celebrate progress, recognise outstanding contribution and encourage continual improvement.
Beyond the curriculum, an extensive programme of clubs, squads, tournaments and competitions enables girls to pursue their passions and perform at the highest level. Our swimmers have achieved exceptional success, becoming London Schools Swimming Champions in 2026 while also competing in the IAPS National Finals. Skiing is another area of distinction, with Glendower crowned winners of the 2026 Schools with Altitude National Ski Championships and regularly competing in the U11 IAPS Championships in Italy.

pageCache.pageTitle: Introduction to Prep - Glendower Preparatory School
pageCache.text:
Introduction to Prep
IN 100 WORDS
The Prep School at Glendower is a time of intellectual growth, increasing independence and expanding opportunity. From Years 3 to 6, girls experience a rich, academically rigorous curriculum taught by specialist teachers, designed to deepen understanding and spark curiosity. Alongside this, they embrace a breadth of opportunities, in sport, the arts, leadership and outdoor learning, that build confidence and character.
As they mature, our pupils develop the skills, resilience and ambition needed for success at 11+ and beyond, leaving us as thoughtful, capable and self-assured girls ready for the next stage of their education.
The Prep School at Glendower is a vibrant and transformative stage in a girl’s educational journey. Spanning Years 3 to 6, it is a time of growing independence, deepening intellectual engagement and expanding horizons.
At the heart of the Prep experience is academic rigour. Our girls benefit from specialist teaching across the curriculum, enabling a depth and quality of learning that both challenges and inspires. Lessons are carefully designed to develop critical thinking, intellectual curiosity and a genuine love of scholarship. Girls are encouraged to ask questions, explore ideas and take pride in the process of learning as much as the outcome.
As pupils move through the Prep School, they take increasing ownership of their learning. They become more organised, reflective and self-directed, developing the habits and mindset that underpin academic success. This progression is carefully supported, ensuring that each girl grows in confidence and capability at a pace that is right for her.
Beyond the classroom, the breadth of opportunity is a defining feature of Prep life at Glendower. Our pupils immerse themselves in a wide range of experiences, from competitive sport and performances in music and drama, to creative arts, clubs and enrichment activities. Educational visits and residential trips further extend learning, offering moments of challenge, adventure and discovery that foster resilience and independence.
Leadership opportunities also play a central role. As the oldest pupils in the school, our Year 6 girls take on positions of responsibility and act as role models for younger pupils. Through these experiences, they develop a strong sense of self, an understanding of service and the confidence to lead with integrity.
Preparation for 11+ is woven thoughtfully into the fabric of the Prep School. Our approach balances high academic expectations with a deep understanding of each pupil as an individual. Through expert teaching, careful guidance and a strong partnership with families, we ensure that every girl is well prepared, not only to achieve excellent outcomes, but to approach the process with confidence and perspective.

pageCache.pageTitle: Introduction to Reception & Pre-Prep - Glendower Preparatory School
pageCache.text:
Introduction to Reception & Pre-Prep
IN 100 WORDS
Reception and Pre-Prep at Glendower lay the foundations for a lifetime of confident, curious and successful learning. Through a carefully structured, age-appropriate curriculum, we combine academic rigour with warmth, creativity and care. Strong relationships between each girl and her teacher ensure that every girl is known and supported to thrive.
Reception and Pre-Prep at Glendower represent an important element in each girl’s development. Spanning Reception to Year 2, these years establish the essential foundations for future academic success while nurturing confidence, curiosity and a love of learning.
Our approach is both rigorous and developmentally appropriate. We place a strong emphasis on early literacy, numeracy, reasoning and communication, ensuring that key skills are taught systematically and with precision. At the same time, learning is engaging, creative and responsive to the needs of each child, allowing girls to develop understanding in a way that feels meaningful and enjoyable.
Central to this phase is the strength of relationships. Each girl is supported by a dedicated teacher and teaching assistant who know her well, academically, socially and emotionally. This close partnership enables us to tailor learning, provide timely support and ensure that every pupil feels secure, valued and ready to take the next steps in her development.
Our Glen 7 readiness programme underpins this journey. Designed to ensure a smooth and successful transition into the Prep School, it brings together academic preparation with a rich breadth of opportunity. Our girls experience a wide range of subjects and activities, including sport, the arts and enrichment, while also developing an understanding of themselves as learners: their strengths, their challenges and how they learn best.
